clue.text: Regulation applied to new part of garden

parts.note: a regulation is a rule, a law

explanation.surface: A rule has been imposed on a freshly laid section of someone's garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassed area of mown turf is a typical feature of a garden.

clue.text: Time to come round about match

indicators.note: coming round something means enclosing it, so the time word wraps the next piece

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
RE is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone waits for the moment a sporting fixture comes round again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a sporting noun but is the verb: to correspond or concur.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that match are in accord, a synonym for concurring.

clue.text: Executive toy used by scientist from birth?

definitions.meaning: a desk gadget of swinging steel balls that click against one another
the bed Isaac Newton the physicist would have slept in as a baby

explanation.surface: A desk gadget is whimsically imagined as something a famous scientist used as an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is playful: the physicist's infant bed, a cradle, is the name of the toy that demonstrates his laws of motion.
explanation.definitionFit: The swinging-ball desk gadget demonstrating momentum is named after the physicist Isaac Newton.

clue.text: Support for sail in good time, without needing a professional

parts.note: a mast is the pole holding a ship's sail

indicators.note: the word for punctual is used minus the article that follows these words

parts.note: arriving in good time means arriving early

explanation.surface: A sailor sets a mast up promptly and manages without hiring an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without needing' takes the A from EARLY, leaving ERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done with skilled expertise, in the adjectival sense of professional, is masterly.

clue.text: It helps me perceive an exclamation of surprise

definitions.meaning: the organ of sight belonging to the speaker
a dated interjection of astonishment or disbelief

explanation.surface: Someone explains what lets them see, then exclaims in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both literally one's own organ of vision and a mild expletive of disbelief.

clue.text: Second loud comment about beard without much substance

indicators.note: placed around, so the shout encloses the beard word

parts.note: a cry is a loud call or remark
an awn is the bristly 'beard' on an ear of barley or other grass

explanation.surface: Someone makes a second loud remark about a wispy, insubstantial beard.
explanation.walkthrough: AWN is the botanical name for the bristles on cereal heads, which are called a beard.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, bony person lacks bulk or flesh, so is insubstantial.

clue.text: Stuff for DIY-er — amount in piles scattered around

indicators.note: items scattered around are strewn in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A home decorator has left heaps of material strewn about the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Water-based wall coating is a staple product for a home decorator.

clue.text: Easy-to-read French articles about British territory

indicators.note: around, so the two articles sit either side of the territory

parts.note: le is a French article; two of them give the pair
Gib is the familiar short name for Gibraltar, a British Overseas Territory

explanation.surface: Some French newspaper pieces about a British overseas territory are clear to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' here are grammatical words, LE and LE, not newspaper pieces; they flank GIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Handwriting that can be deciphered easily is clear, which is the plain synonym here.

clue.text: Picture of listener? Come close

parts.note: a picture of something is it drawn, as in sketched
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: An artist offers a sketch of an ear and invites someone nearer to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach or move nearer is to come close, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Encourage heading away from sudden rise in water

indicators.note: the head of the word, its first letter, is taken away

parts.note: a surge is a sudden swell of sea or river water

explanation.surface: Someone is told to move away from a rising tide.
explanation.definitionFit: To press or spur someone on is to urge them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Not very close regarding small item

parts.note: RE means regarding, as in a letter heading
a mote is a tiny speck or particle

explanation.surface: Something small is described as not near at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant places are far away, the plain sense of remote.

clue.text: Sure — football will involve one

indicators.note: the words that follow contain the answer inside them, so their letters are searched

explanation.surface: Someone confidently says a football match will need an official.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'suRE Football'; 'one' is the definition, the official football involves.
explanation.definitionFit: One here means an official who football matches always include: the referee.

clue.text: Accompaniment to sushi: was sailor given one?

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common crossword sailor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether a seaman was handed a portion of the green condiment with his sushi.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot green Japanese horseradish paste is served alongside sushi.

clue.text: Commemorative envelope from factory drives production

indicators.note: producing something means making it anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A souvenir envelope comes out of a plant that pushes output.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp collectors prize an envelope franked on the day a new stamp issue appears.

clue.text: Reluctance to move, i.e. train broken down

indicators.note: something broken down is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A locomotive that has failed shows no willingness to go anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics names the tendency of a body to resist a change of motion; figuratively, sluggishness.

clue.text: Failure has gone wrong, leading to pique

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to work

indicators.note: gone wrong means awry, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A failed attempt has misfired, and resentment follows.
explanation.definitionFit: In high indignation or resentment, one is in a fit of pique.

clue.text: Sun god linked to unknown quantity of sunlight

parts.note: Ra is the ancient Egyptian sun god
y is a conventional algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An Egyptian deity is associated with an unmeasured amount of daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: A single beam is the small amount meant by a glimmer of daylight.

clue.text: Forecaster getting editor to show anger

parts.note: a seer foretells the future

explanation.surface: A weather or fortune forecaster gets a newspaper boss to lose their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To become furious is an idiom built on the colour associated with rage.

clue.text: Deliver drink before work

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink before starting the day's job.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish or provide goods is to deliver them.

clue.text: Picked up this when taking in good view

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
taking in means enclosing, so the word this wraps the next piece

explanation.surface: Someone collected this on taking in a fine panorama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts as a sound indicator, but in this down clue it lifts THGIS, i.e. THIS round G, upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or spectacle worth seeing is a sight, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Vassal that is restricted by broken leg

indicators.note: held within, so the first piece is confined by the other
a broken limb is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A feudal servant is laid up by a fractured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vassal' is the definition: the word serves for both the feudal lord and the subject owing him service.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudally the word can mean a subject owing allegiance as well as the lord owed it.

clue.text: Boss curtailed educational activity

indicators.note: a tail cut off means the final letter of the word goes

parts.note: study is learning activity

explanation.surface: An employer cut short a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager, but here it is a knob or stud, a raised ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised ornamental knob, as is a decorative stud.

clue.text: Kitchen device, say — good range, on reflection

parts.note: e.g., for example, is signalled by say

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a remit is the range of one's responsibility

explanation.surface: A cooker is offered as an example of a decent kitchen range, after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' tempts as the cooker, but it is REMIT, the scope of duties, reversed to TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand-glass for boiling breakfast eggs is a classic piece of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Vegetarian food: obscure line taken by aficionado

parts.note: to haze is to obscure, as with mist
a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A dim line of vegetarian produce has been adopted by an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible kernel of a hedgerow tree is a meat-free food.

clue.text: Trio ignoring hot part of forest

indicators.note: leaving something out, so that letter is dropped from the number

parts.note: a trio is three
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Three walkers avoid the hot section of the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is made up of many individual woody plants.
